MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 11, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:00 p.m., on April 11, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 6, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley (arrived at 5:02)
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Goodell declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

CONSIDERATION OF ADDITION OF LATE ARISING MATTER

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that a matter arose after the agenda was posted and that there
is a need for the Council to consider a late item regarding a resolution for funding from the Forest
Health Grant Program for brush control and removal.

City Council Minutes  1  April 11, 2023
 Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum to walk this
item on the agenda to be discussed under New Business.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim April 2023 To Be National Donate Life Month

  Mayor Goodell presented proclamation to Leslie Eskildsen ~ OneLegacy Ambassador.

P2. Proclaim the Week of April 9 through 15, 2023 To Be National Public Safety
  Telecommunicators Week

  Mayor Goodell presented proclamation to OCFA Battalion Chief Jason Taylor.

P3. Vector Control Update

  Received presentation by Vector Control Director Lora Young.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gideon Victor, M.V.: Spoke on an analytical map on income statement of property taxes , sales
taxes, and revenues. Offered his services on the analysis.

Michelle O’Brien, M.V.: Spoke about the Corp Yard project specifically the eight-million-dollar
access road and voiced concerns about the cost. She reminded residents that Earth and Arbor Day
is April 22 along with National Prescription Drug Take Back Day. Lastly, she thanked the City
Council for recognizing Donate Life Month and informed the Council that her brother recently
passed away and his generous gift has changed seventy-five lives including wounded veterans and
first responders.

Andrew Correces, M.V.: Spoke on rat poison being used by his homeowner’s association in his
condominium complex and voiced concerns of the danger of these poisons. Stated he would like
to see it illegal in the State.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Spoke on the approval of a purchase of two gas vehicles for the Animal
Services Department at the last meeting. He questioned why the City is still pursuing gas vehicles
City Council Minutes  2  April 11, 2023
 as opposed to electric vehicles and asked that the City adopt a policy that all future vehicle
replacements be electric like the cities of Newport Beach and Irvine.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on the ULI report and asked if we are using this as a guide. Questioned
that some of concepts being considered were not in the original study and asked for a specific plan.

LaVal Brewer, M.V.: Introduced himself to the City Council and stated he is the President of
Orange County Community Outreach and said that he has applied for the Planning Commission
and outlined his experience.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Spoke on his conversation with Avalon Bay regarding the Garden Plaza.
Stated building a high-rise development will cause heavy traffic, noise pollution, and safety issues.
Asked if a pre-application has been filed for this potential project. Lastly, he suggested we restore
the Garden Plaza and bring back small businesses which can be accomplished if the City purchases
the property.

Lynn Holmes, M.V.: Stated that she hoped we can make the Garden Plaza a marvelous corner that
increases the things that residents want as well as incorporating some things that the State requires.
She expressed that the architecture should be consistent with our City. She voiced concerns of a
repeat of the Stop the Monster.

Wendy Lee, M.V.: Spoke on high risk areas that are unable to get fire insurance for single family
homes and asked that the city advocate for single family homes with the State Insurance
Commissioner. Asked that the City advocate for the single-family home’s insurance.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 14 and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the regular City Council Minutes for the Meeting of April 11, 2023, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated March 17, 2023 in the Amount of $753,080.69

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated March 24, 2023 in the Amount of $798,067.87
City Council Minutes  3  April 11, 2023
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated March 17, 2023 in the Amount of $19,041.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated March 24, 2023 in the Amount of $30,826.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2023

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for February 2023

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for February 2023

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2023

  Received and filed.

10. California Yellow Cab Contract Amendment for Senior Mobility Program

  Approved First Amendment to California Yellow Cab Agreement for Services with the
  Senior Mobility Program.

11. Draft 2023-2024 Annual Action Plan Detailing the Proposed Use of Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds

  Adopted Resolution 23-12 approving the City's 2023-2024 Annual Action Plan detailing the
  proposed use of Community Development Block Grant Funds, and authorizing submission
  of the plan to the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development.

12. Melinda Road Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 23837)

  Approved bid specifications, subject to technical revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

City Council Minutes  4  April 11, 2023
 13. La Paz Bridge/Road Widening (CIP 756) - SCE Street Light Modifications

  Authorized payment in the amount of $48,912.58 to Southern California Edison Company
  for street lighting system modifications associated with the La Paz Bridge/Road Widening
  project (CIP 756).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

14. Madrid Fore Park Play Area Rehabilitation - CIP 334

  Director of Public Services Jerry Hill answered questions from Council Members.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Goodell, to (1) award
  contract A23-15 and approved issuance of Purchase Order to Micon Construction, Inc. for
  the Madrid Fore Park Play Area Rehabilitation-CIP 334 in an amount not to exceed
  $822,781.00; (2) approve issuance of Purchase Order for the purchase of a shade structure,
  Berliner and Playworld Playground equipment to Dave Bang Associates, Inc. in the amount
  not to exceed $307,108.69; (3) approve issuance of Purchase Order for the purchase of
  Security Lighting Ameron Poles to Ameron Pole Products in the amount not to exceed
  $62,015.00; (4) approve issuance of Purchase Order for the purchase of Security Lighting
  Fixtures to Lighting Supply Guy in the amount not to exceed $56,720.14; and (5) approve
  issuance of Purchase Order for the purchase of GameTime Playground Equipment to Great
  Western Recreation in the amount not to exceed $38,448.46.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15. Felipe Road & Oso Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP 16224)

  Director of Public Works explained the improvements and answered Council Member’s
  questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  authorize the approval of Change Order 1 to Purchase Order 21900431 to Michael Baker
  International, Inc. in the amount of $55,996 for additional design services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  April 11, 2023
 NEW BUSINESS

16A. Consideration of Resolution for Grant Funding from the State Department of
  Forestry and Fire Protection

  Director of Public Services Jerry Hill presented a report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to adopt
  Resolution 23-13 for Funding from the Forest Health Grant Program as Provided Through
  the Greenhouse Reduction Fund.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16. FY 2023-2025 Revenue Projections

  Director of Administrative Services presented the staff report.

  By consensus the City Council received and filed the report.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17. Appointment of City Commission Members

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to appoint
  Ross Kezelman to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to appoint
  LaVal Brewer to the Planning & Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  April 11, 2023
   Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to appoint
  Brent Cranmer to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CITY MANAGER REPORT

18. Housing Law Overview

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Wendy Lee, M.V.: Stated that almost every city in California was denied their housing
  elements. Spoke on the new housing laws that are giving density bonuses and that it has
  become very anti-single-family homes.  She encouraged residents to go to
  www.socialprogress.org/index/california where one can find how their neighborhood is rated
  and she outlined the ratings. Lastly, she stated that home ownership is the American Dream
  and it is being threatened.

  Council Member Bucknum requested that the objective design standards on developments
  come before the Council at a future meeting.

  City Manager Wilberg stated that to jump start the hiring process of a consultant we would
  need to advance funding out of reserves of approximately $150,000. He indicated that Elaine
  has consultant proposals ready to come back at the next meeting.

  City Attorney Curley stated that the purpose of objective design standards is for the quality
  or design characteristics that the City wants for future developments.

  By consensus the City Council received and filed the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended an Iftar Dinner which is the meal eaten
after sunset during Ramadan at our local Mosque. She attended the Marine Appreciation Day at
Lake Mission Viejo this past weekend. She reminded residents that this Saturday is the Spring
City Council Minutes  7  April 11, 2023
 Boutique at the Norman P. Community Center and that Tax Day has been pushed to October by
the Governor. Council Member Bucknum stated that volunteer planting will take place on April
22 in honor of Arbor Day. She hoped everyone had a Happy Easter and stated that she spent the
day at the Montanoso Recreation Center on The Deck. She announced she has an Orange County
Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) meeting tomorrow and will be in Sacramento
next Monday and Tuesday for a conference with the California Association of Governments
(SCAG).

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch gave kudos to Marine Adoption Committee’s Gail Wood on all the work
she does for this committee. He attended the Vietnam War Veteran Commemorating Ceremony
along with Mayor Pro Tem Kelley and had the great honor of pinning a defense award to one of
our retired marines and indicated that it was one of the most things he has ever done. Lastly, he
attended a pickleball player luncheon

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez said she also attended the Interfaith Iftar Dinner and an Animal Shelter
tour and expressed that the staff is doing a fantastic job. She went to Capo Unified School District’s
EOC tour and stated that they have a great plan in place in the event of an emergency. She also
attended the Vietnam War Veteran Commemorative Ceremony and was given a star from a
decommissioned flag that was previously flown at Miramar National Cemetery which is where her
father is buried so she expressed great appreciation. She attended a Easter Egg Hunt at Coronado
Park. Council Member Vasquez indicated that her family spent Easter at her sister’s home in San
Diego and that her daughter won the Easter egg dying contest.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she also attended the Iftar Dinner as well as De Portola
Elementary School’s 50th Anniversary. She attended the Vietnam War Veteran Commemorative
Ceremony and was also able to pin one of the Veterans. She went to Coffee with a Cop which
was held on April 5 with Deputy Murphy and Chief McDonald as well as other Police Services
staff. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked the Marine Adoption Committee for the Marine
Appreciation Day at Lake Mission Viejo. She explained that the City adopted the Headquarters
Battalion First Marine Division Camp Pendleton in 2006, which comprises of 1400 marines. She
stated it was a well-attended event. She informed residents that the next park to be renovated is
Crucero Park and stated she has had a number of requests for renovation of this park. Next year
Barbadanes Park will be renovated. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that the Community
of Character will be celebrating their 20th Anniversary and the Character Word of the Month for
April is Service.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell announced that he went on a tour of the Marguerite Aquatics Center and the Oso
Creek Club House with Supervisor Don Wagner and his staff. He mentioned that this upcoming
weekend he will be departing to Australia and he showed the sports brochure he will be taking
City Council Minutes  8  April 11, 2023
 with him along with some other gifts for dignitaries. Mayor Goodell showed the introduction
video.

ADJOURNMENT AT 9:11 PM TO TUESDAY, APRIL 25, 2023, AT 5:00 P.M.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 25, 2023

City Council Minutes  9  April 11, 2023
